name: Banh canh ghe
summary: Bánh canh ghẹ is thick rice or tapioca noodles in a crab broth. Vietnam Tourism simmers crab shells with coconut milk and spices, and finishes the bowl with crab meat, herbs, fried shallots, and lime. Vietnam Airlines does not mention coconut milk. Both stay.
origin: Vung Tau, on Vietnam Tourism’s local-eating article. Vietnam Airlines names Tú Xương, Võ Thị Sáu, and Lê Lai.
texture: Vietnam Tourism calls the noodles thick and chewy, and the broth creamy. Vietnam Airlines calls the noodles soft and chewy and the broth lightly thick.
taste: Vietnam Tourism ties the broth to crab shells, coconut milk, and spices, and calls it umami. Vietnam Airlines ties the sweetness to bones and crab, with pepper, scallion, and greens. The heading says ghẹ. One caption on the same Vietnam Airlines article says cua. Keep both words, and keep the coconut milk.
howToEat: Eat it from the bowl. Lime is on the Vietnam Tourism account. Pepper, scallion, and greens are on the Vietnam Airlines account.
Vietnam Airlines prints 60,000–120,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Tú Xương, Võ Thị Sáu, and Lê Lai. A shop name is not published here. The hour is Check on arrival.
priceBand: Vietnam Airlines prints 60,000–120,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism printed no price.
seoTitle: Banh canh ghe — crab noodles in Vung Tau
seoDescription: Crab bánh canh in Vung Tau. Vietnam Tourism includes coconut milk. Vietnam Airlines prints 60,000–120,000 VND and does not mention coconut milk.
